methods: locating and classifying the critical point
statement: For $x>0$ let $f(x)=x^{1/x}$. By taking logarithms, show that $f$ attains its maximum at $x=e$ and find the maximum value of $f$.
solution:
Set $y=x^{1/x}$; then $\\ln y=\\frac{\\ln x}{x}$. Differentiating, $\\frac{y'}{y}=\\frac{1-\\ln x}{x^{2}}$, so $y'=x^{1/x}\\frac{1-\\ln x}{x^{2}}$. This vanishes only when $\\ln x=1$, i.e. $x=e$. For $x<e$ we have $\\ln x<1$ so $y'>0$, and for $x>e$ we have $y'<0$; hence $f$ has a maximum at $x=e$. The maximum value is $f(e)=e^{1/e}$.
